title: Realtime fallbacks & session windowing demo - HelioPay
summary: Demo focused on long-context session windowing, streaming backpressure behavior, and realtime fallbacks under high TPS. Walked through API, Console traces, and Optimize recommendations. Agreed next steps: run a 10k synthetic TPS pilot, share region capacity and pricing, and provide SOC2 + KMS notes.

transcript:
Header: Date: 2027-09-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 56 mins | Attendees: Jordan (AE), Samira (SE), Liam (Solutions Eng) — Priya (Lead ML), Markus (SRE), Ravi (Product)

Auto-summary: Quick demo showing how Redwood handles long session windows and falls back under stream pressure; showed Console traces and Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization.

Topics: session windowing, streaming backpressure, fallback routing, long context KV caching, pilot sizing

00:00 Jordan (AE): Alright hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE for HelioPay. Samira will run the demo and Liam will chime in on runbooks and Optimize.
00:22 Priya (Customer): Hi all, Priya here. We're mostly concerned with sessions that keep growing - users who keep adding context over long chats — and what happens when we push to like high TPS bursts during peak.
00:35 Samira (SE): Great, we'll start with the API behavior for a long context session then jump into the Console traces and Optimize recs. Quick note: I'll show both hosted and a dedicated fallback path.
00:48 Markus (Customer): We also need to understand timeouts — we have 800ms P95 SLA on a critical path; curious where Redwood sits with streaming and timeouts.
01:02 Samira: Yep, important. We'll show P50/P95 numbers, and the streaming backpressure behavior — including how the KV cash, sorry K-V cache, gets evicted and how session windowing reduces cold-start tokens.
01:20 Ravi (Customer): "KV cash" made me laugh — transcription will do that.
01:25 [laughter]
01:30 Samira: Okay demo: showing API request stream — sending a 30k token session, mixed history, with repeated prefix prompts to test prefix caching. Watch Console -> Traces -> Streams.
01:45 [screen share noise]
02:05 Samira: Console shows our runtime selected a quantized variant for this model because sequence length is long, that's an Optimize recommendation to keep cost down. Notice the kernel selection changed at token ~8k to a long-seq kernel.
02:32 Priya: Is that deterministic across hardware? We run on a mix of NVLink and some older A100s.
02:40 Samira: Good question. Kernel selection is runtime-driven — it'll pick the optimal kernel available and we surface which kernel in trace metadata. On older hardware it picks a different kernel but same correctness.
02:55 Jordan: Also worth noting routing policies — we can pin routing by region or by cost tier; for HelioPay we can ensure primary route on Dedicated for critical flows and fallback to Hosted less-critical flows.
03:12 Markus: Show the fallback behavior under surge — we want to see graceful degradation not hard failures.
03:20 Samira: I'll induce a synthetic TPS spike while maintaining the long session, watch the stream for backpressure events.
03:33 [typing / load test starts]
04:00 Samira: Spike started. See at 04:05 the stream latency slowly increases — we hit a batching threshold and the runtime starts coalescing tokens. At 04:22 you see the router trigger a fallback to a smaller quantized model for non-critical routes.
04:35 Priya: How do you classify non-critical? Our payments confirmation flow is critical.
04:40 Samira: You mark routes in the API call or via Console routing rules — e.g., header x-helio-critical: true — Redwood respects that and will keep critical flows on dedicated pool with no model variant fallback unless capacity exhausted and you allow a graceful fallback policy.
05:00 Markus: What's the timeout behavior for streaming partial responses? If we drop a chunk, will the client get a 504 or partial stream?
05:10 Liam (Solutions Eng): By default you'll see a stream-shedding signal — the SDK surfaces a 'chunk-dropped' event and the stream will close with a structured error. We also support an automatic retry to a warm fallback model within the same session so you can continue conversation albeit with a slightly smaller context preserved.
05:34 Priya: That automatic retry — does it preserve KV cache?
05:38 Samira: We attempt KV snapshotting for warm handoffs. It's best-effort; large KV snapshots may be truncated. That's where session windowing comes in — you define a retention policy to keep the most relevant spans in memory so handoffs are smaller.
05:58 Priya: Hmm ok. Can we set retention by token count or by semantic score?
06:05 Samira: Both — Console Optimize suggests a token-window and an importance-rank window. For HelioPay's pattern we recommend a 12k token sliding window with semantic thinning of older history.
06:20 Priya: Nice. Show the Console policy UI.
06:25 [screen share: Console -> Routing -> Windowing policy]
06:38 Samira: Here you can preview the session before and after thinning; the Optimize tab shows estimated cost delta and expected P95 improvement. For this demo, thinning reduced cold-start tokens by ~40% and P95 by ~120ms.
06:58 Markus: Can you run a high TPS sim — like 10k TPS — and show how fallback routing behaves end-to-end?
07:05 Samira: We'll run a mixed workload: 80% short requests (<=512 tokens) and 20% long sessions (10k tokens). Starting the synthetic harness now.
07:22 [load test ramp-up sounds]
07:45 Samira: Ramp reached 10k TPS. Console trace shows queueing at the batching layer at 07:50, TTL for some streaming chunks hits and we start returning 'partial' flags. See the trace event 'backpressure: coalesce'.
08:02 Ravi: Are partial flags visible to product? We want to surface to UX that the response is partial and will continue or fallback.
08:10 Liam: SDK has hooks to flag partial/continued; we recommend product add UI affordances — spinner + 'continued' badge.
08:18 Markus: On the SRE side, what metrics should we watch? Queue length, batch latency, token throughput?
08:25 Samira: Exactly: inflight_batches, batch_latency_p95, kv_eviction_rate, router_fallback_rate. We showed those in Console's topology view earlier.
08:40 Priya: I saw a 'router_fallback_rate' spike to 12% — what's acceptable?
08:47 Samira: For critical payments flows you'd want <1%. For mixed workloads, 5% is common depending on cost tradeoffs.
09:00 Jordan: This is where dedicated reserved capacity helps — keeps fallback low. We'll share committed capacity numbers.
09:08 Priya: Also curious about encryption while snapshotting KV — we need KMS integration.
09:14 Samira: We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated; snapshots are encrypted at rest with per-customer keys. We'll attach the KMS integration doc to the follow-up.
09:30 Markus: Can you show a real example where a long session crosses regional boundaries and how handoffs work? We use multi-region for redundancy.
09:40 Samira: Quick example: session pinned to us-east during initial flow; on region overload we route to eu-west fallback with explicit migration policy. The KV snapshot is transferred via encrypted transit and then rehydrated — there will be a small token loss depending on snapshot size.
10:05 Priya: How visible is that token loss to the app? Can we detect truncation?
10:10 Liam: Trace events annotate 'rehydration_truncation' with counts; your app can choose to re-ask a short summarization prompt to recover.
10:22 [brief crosstalk]
10:30 Samira: Next, Optimize recommendations: batching knob suggestions, quantization variant, and model sizing by throughput. For HelioPay we suggested two gpus dedicated + 20% burst to handle 10k TPS mixed workload with expected P95 ~420ms on short requests.
10:52 Priya: That P95 seems ok. What about long sessions P95?
10:56 Samira: Long sessions are dominated by per-token generation and KV overhead; with session windowing we measured P95 for a 10k token continuation at ~2.4s for token streaming and end-to-end response about 3.1s in our sim.
11:14 Markus: And if we need lower latency we can move critical flows to smaller context models?
11:19 Samira: Exactly — tradeoff is small context model reduces context window but improves latency/cost. You can use hybrid routing: critical short flows to a low-latency model, long assistant convos to a high-capacity model.
11:34 Ravi: Any notes about billing when fallback occurs? We don't want surprises.
11:39 Jordan: Billing ties to the model variant and token counts processed. Fallback to a smaller model typically reduces cost; but if you have reserved capacity there are committed fees. We'll send a clear example in the pricing sheet.
11:55 Priya: Ok let's talk failure modes — streaming timeouts, chunk corruption etc.
12:02 Samira: We logged a couple examples earlier: chunk duplication, partial chunk, and chunk loss. SDKs provide idempotency keys for resuming; the Console will show 'stream_recovery' attempts with timestamps.
12:20 Markus: Will the system retry automatically? We prefer explicit control vs automatic retries to avoid duplicate charges.
12:25 Liam: Retry policy is configurable per route — default is conservative: one internal retry to a warm fallback model, no billing duplication for retried tokens in most cases, but we'll outline exact billing semantics in follow-up.
12:42 [20 min mark: mid-demo Q&A, then deeper technical runbook conversation]
33:01 Priya: For the pilot, can we get a small dedicated pool isolated for payments + a shared pool for background tasks?
33:10 Jordan: Yes, you can have multiple pools and explicit routing. We'll propose a two-pool setup in the pilot doc.
33:25 Markus: Can we instrument a synthetic that mimics our users — 70% short, 20% medium, 10% very long — and replay real session patterns?
33:34 Samira: Absolutely, we'll run the synthetic using your sample trace. Please upload a 24h sample to the S3 link we'll provide.
33:45 Priya: Security checklist — SOC2, ISO, SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs. We need to see retention controls as well.
33:55 Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 + security pack. For retention, you control session retention policies and export/delete hooks.
34:08 Rahul [off-channel?]: (inaudible)
34:12 [slight noise]
34:20 Samira: Quick recap of observed behaviors: fallback policy worked and routed non-critical flows to quantized fallback; session windowing reduced cold tokens and improved P95; backpressure events surfaced in Console with actionable metrics.
34:38 Priya: That aligns with our needs. A couple concerns — KV snapshot size and cross-region rehydration time.
34:48 Liam: We'll produce size estimates and a runbook for rehydration; generally aim to keep per-session snapshot under ~4MB for fast transfer.
35:05 Priya: Perfect. Next steps?
35:10 Jordan: Action items as we discussed — we'll run the 10k TPS synthetic next week, share pricing and SOC docs, and schedule an SRE deep dive.
35:20 Markus: Good. Thanks team.
35:28 [meeting end small chatter]
35:40 Jordan: Thanks everyone, end of demo.
